messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: what causes errors printed when running Winston's Gist 4211337?
parts:
Hi Vincent -

Those errors are coming up because at first, the values of input$dataset and input$columns aren't set -- there has to be a bit of back and forth between the server and the client before those values are set. It's also the reason that there are some error messages that are briefly visible in the browser.

I've modified the gist to add some checks for NULL. In the output functions, it checks if the inputs are NULL; if so, then the output functions just returns. This removes the errors at the console, as well as the errors in the browser.
runGist('4211337')

https://gist.github.com/4211337


-Winston

messages.subject: Re: what causes errors printed when running Winston's Gist 4211337?
parts:
Oh, strange, it should be fixed now. Thanks for pointing that out.

It looks like, as part of their revamping of the gist pages, Github has changed the way that pushing to gists works. In the past I've used this process to edit gists: clone the gist to a local repository, edit the files, commit, then push. But it looks like pushing to a gist doesn't work properly anymore -- it updates the remote repository, but the gist webpage doesn't show the new changes. I now see this when I push to a gist repo:

remote: WARN The dotcom gem environment is out-of-date or has yet to be bootstrapped.
remote:      Run script/bootstrap to remedy this situation.
remote: /data/github/current/config/basic.rb:98: gem environment not configured (RuntimeError)
remote: from hooks/post-receive:12:in `require'
remote: from hooks/post-receive:12

My guess is that this is the post-receive hook for updating the gist webpage. So it appears that, for the changes to show in the webpage, the gist must be edited from the web interface (which I've done for this example).

-Winston
On Wed, Jan 2, 2013 at 11:05 AM, Vincent <vincen...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks for the explanation Winston. I looked at the Gist but didn't see any changes. Am I missing something?


On Wednesday, January 2, 2013 8:10:20 AM UTC-8, Winston Chang wrote:
Hi Vincent -

Those errors are coming up because at first, the values of input$dataset and input$columns aren't set -- there has to be a bit of back and forth between the server and the client before those values are set. I've modified the gist to add some checks for NULL. In the output functions, it checks if the inputs are NULL; if so, then the output functions just returns. This removes the errors at the console, as well as the errors in the browser.
runGist('4211337')

https://gist.github.com/4211337
